title: Delight in the will and movements of the appetite
source_text: XXXVII. In hoc genere quoque ponunt interiorem quandam delectationem in voluntate, ex ejusmodi illustrationibus sequi solitam. Et praeterea varios motus qui divinitus excitantur in appetitu: qualia sunt amor, timor, spes, dolor, & confusio, & similes affectiones, quibus trahitur, & inclinatur interdum ratio superior, ut virtutem sectetur, & declinet vitia.
pass_a_gloss: XXXVII. In this kind also they place a certain interior delight in the will, wont to follow from illuminations of this kind. And besides various motions which are divinely excited in the appetite: such as are love, fear, hope, sorrow, and confusion, and like affections, by which the higher reason is drawn, and inclined at times, to follow virtue, and shun vices.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXVII. Under this heading they also place an inner delight in the will, which usually follows such enlightenments.

They add various movements that God stirs up in the appetite, such as love, fear, hope, sorrow, shame and similar feelings. By these the higher reason is sometimes drawn and inclined to pursue virtue and turn away from vice.

choices.why: The scholastic pair: grace that rouses and calls, and grace that helps the will to will and to act; kept as in the previous packet.
